items.title: CVE-2026-120322 — A vulnerability was identified in Termix-SSH Termix up to 2.9.2. This issue affects some u…
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-120322 (score CVSS 9.9).

A vulnerability was identified in Termix-SSH Termix up to 2.9.2. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /plugin-api/file-manager/transferToHost. The manipulation of the argument destPath leads to path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The shortcut was removed in the standalone File Manager plugin v1.0.0 (transfer engine now always writes over SFTP) and in core v26.10.0.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-120322 (score CVSS 9.9).

A vulnerability was identified in Termix-SSH Termix up to 2.9.2. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /plugin-api/file-manager/transferToHost. The manipulation of the argument destPath leads to path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The shortcut was removed in the standalone File Manager plugin v1.0.0 (transfer engine now always writes over SFTP) and in core v26.10.0. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

items.title: Pentagon investigates suspected cyberattack on military base freezers
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique.

The Pentagon is investigating a suspected cyberattack involving refrigeration systems at at least six U.S. military bases, according to Reuters. The malfunctions occurred in August at military commissaries, where freezer temperatures unexpectedly increased, spoiling food. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, officials reported that a freezer entered defrost mode overnight, heating its contents rather than maintaining safe storage temperatures.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique.

The Pentagon is investigating a suspected cyberattack involving refrigeration systems at at least six U.S. military bases, according to Reuters. The malfunctions occurred in August at military commissaries, where freezer temperatures unexpectedly increased, spoiling food. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, officials reported that a freezer entered defrost mode overnight, heating its contents rather than maintaining safe storage temperatures. The investigation follows a confirmed cyberattack on commercial refrigeration systems at more than 350 establishments in France earlier this month. ㅤ Experts with Xcape, BreachLock, Suzu Labs and Finite State offer perspectives on the matter. ㅤ Damon Small, Board Member, Xcape, Inc. “Compromising industrial refrigeration systems transforms routine facility hardware into an immediate operational liability, spoiling vital food supplies and disrupting logistics across military bases. While refrigeration devices may seem an unlikely target, the reality of the situation is that attackers are often opportunistic. The question we have to ask is whether these and other incidents against industrial cooling units are targeted to cause panic and damage, or if it is simply a matter of adversaries finding a new attack path. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Global Sec Mag.

Pour donner suite à l'annonce du piratage de la plateforme spécialisée en cryptomonnaies Binance, évalué à 6,3 milliards de dollars, ce qui représente un nouveau record, les commentaires de Samuel Hassine, CEO de Filigran : « Le chiffre record fera les gros titres, mais c'est le point d'entrée banal qui constitue la vraie leçon. Binance indique que l'attaque aurait pu démarrer avec l'ordinateur portable compromis d'un ingénieur, utilisé pour atteindre un service qui soumet les retraits. L'entreprise a depuis identifié d'autres points de compromission. Selon ses propres déclarations, aucune clé de portefeuille n'a été volée. L'impact est estimé à environ 6,3 milliards de dollars, soit quatre fois le précédent record. Environ 3 milliards de dollars ont été gelés en quelques heures, avec l'aide de partenaires et des forces de l'ordre. Cette coordination est ce qui fonctionne bien. Toute entreprise dont les systèmes déplacent de l'argent sur instruction devrait savoir exactement quelles machines et quels comptes peuvent déclencher un transfert. Il faut partir du principe que l'un d'eux sera un jour compromis, et vérifier que les contrôles en aval tiennent bon. Les vols records commencent par des points d'entrée ordinaires. » Samuel Hassine, CEO et cofondateur, Filigran

items.title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from Binance in 20 minutes
items.body:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Global Sec Mag.

Hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what is believed to be the biggest crypto theft in history. The majority of the stolen assets were transferred within approximately 20 minutes on October 29. Binance initially suspected a compromised employee laptop but subsequently identified additional points of breach.
items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Global Sec Mag.

Hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what is believed to be the biggest crypto theft in history. The majority of the stolen assets were transferred within approximately 20 minutes on October 29. Binance initially suspected a compromised employee laptop but subsequently identified additional points of breach. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs reported that attackers compromised Binance's transaction-signing infrastructure, allowing them to authorize unauthorized transfers from the exchange's wallets. TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the attack to North Korean hackers, citing similarities to previous cryptocurrency thefts, including the $1.5 billion Bybit breach in 2025. Binance has not independently confirmed who was responsible. Stablecoin issuers including Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial moved to freeze approximately half of the stolen assets, with Tether freezing nearly $1.57 billion and Circle more than $800 million. However, researchers estimate approximately $2.4 billion in bitcoin and ether remains beyond the reach of issuer-level freezes. Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover customer losses using its $1 billion protection fund and company resources. ㅤ An expert with Black Hills Information Security offers perspective on the matter. ㅤ John St

Le 1er novembre 2026, le cybercriminel utilisant le pseudonyme necrozma a annoncé la mise en vente d’une base attribuée au célèbre portail immobilier. Mais l’analyse des premiers éléments soulève une question : s’agit-il réellement de données volées ou d’informations déjà publiques ?

Créé en 2015, Bien’ici est l’un des principaux portails immobiliers français . La plateforme permet de rechercher des biens à vendre ou à louer, notamment grâce à une cartographie interactive en 3D. Elle travaille avec plus de 15 000 agences immobilières et professionnels du secteur.

Dans sa publication du 1er novembre 2026 à 20 h 50 , necrozma affirme avoir compromis l’intégralité d’une base de données en exploitant une vulnérabilité de type IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) , accessible sans authentification.

Ce type de faille permet, lorsqu’un contrôle d’accès est défaillant, de consulter des ressources normalement protégées en manipulant leurs identifiants. Elle peut conduire à une exposition massive de données lorsque des informations privées deviennent accessibles sans autorisation.

Le pirate présente un échantillon de 26 fiches d’agences immobilières contenant leurs noms, adresses, numéros de téléphone, informations légales, coordonnées géographiques et listes de collaborateurs.

items.detail:
Signal de veille — SANS ISC.

Recently, I had to extract embedded files from a set of OneNote files (extension .one). My onedump.py tool can extract individual files, so I would have to run this many times. To avoid this, I added a new feature to my onedump.py tool: producing JSON data. Several of my tools already have such a feature : they produce JSON data with the content of their analysis results. onedump's option --jsonoutput produces JSON output with the content of each embedded file found inside the OneNote file. And it can do this for many .one files in one go: onedump.py --jsonoutput *.one To write these files to disk you can use my myjson-filter.py tool, like this: onedump.py --jsonoutput *.one | myjson-filter.py -W hashvir This will write all the embedded files to disk, their name will be the sha256 hash of their content plus extension .vir (hashvir).   Didier Stevens Senior handler blog.DidierStevens.com (c) SANS Internet Storm Center. https://isc.sans.edu Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License.

Signal de veille — CyberScoop.

A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit from the federal government seeking to preemptively block Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola from assuming office if she wins her race. The Department of Justice sued Alaska last month, arguing that an alleged scheme by Peltola to recruit Daniel J. Sullivan, an independent candidate who shares a name with incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, would confuse voters. Peltola’s campaign, the Democratic Senate Campaign Committee and civic groups including the League of Women Voters of Alaska and Common Cause all filed motions to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing the federal government lacks standing and constitutional authority to weigh in on Alaska’s elections. They also said the court cannot grant relief because there is no legal way to determine whether a voter mistakenly voted for one Sullivan over the other without violating the secret ballot. U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason reached the same conclusion, noting in an order “the absence of any explanation from the United States as to how its requested relief could redress its alleged injury while simultaneously maintaining the secrecy of the ballot.” She also wrote that she “cannot grant the United States the relief it seeks because the United States has failed to establish the redressability prerequisite for Article III standing.” Gleason’s opinion recounts Daniel J. Halloween steht vor der Tür. Für Cloudian genau der richtige Zeitpunkt, um Gruselgeschichten rund um Künstliche Intelligenz zu erzählen. Spoiler Alert: Der führende Anbieter von Object Storage und zentrale Player bei modernen KI-Infrastrukturen hat natürlich für jede Horrorstory ein Happy End parat. Es gibt kaum etwas Schöneres, als sich bei Kerzenschein Geschichten zu erzählen. Gerade die kalte und düstere Jahreszeit lädt allerdings eher zu gruseligen Anekdoten ein. Passend dazu hat auch Cloudian gleich sieben Horrorstories vorbereitet, mit der sich Unternehmen aktuell auseinandersetzen müssen. Shadow AI: Der Geist im Prompt Excel-Listen, Verträge und Kundendaten wandern in vielen Unternehmen „nur kurz zur Analyse” zu ChatGPT, Claude & Co. und damit in die USA. Lokal werden LLMs wegen Ressourcenmangel jedenfalls eher selten betrieben. Ob die Daten dann ins Training der KI der großen Anbieter einfließen und von ihr in zweiter Instanz Dritten bereitgestellt werden? Keiner weiß es, wenn der Geist erst einmal aus der Flasche gelassen wurde. Das Happy End für diese Gruselgeschichte sind freigegebene Enterprise-Zugänge mit klaren Datenverarbeitungsbedingungen und Richtlinien, die Mitarbeitende wirklich verstehen, sowie eine kontrollierte Datenbasis im eigenen Haus. items.detail:
Signal de veille — Global Sec Mag.

Laut Trends in Acces Controllers Report 2026 prägen Interoperabilität, Cloud-Anbindung und KI langfristige Zutrittskontrollstrategien Mercury Security, ein weltweit führender Anbieter offener Hardware-Architekturen für Zutrittskontrollsysteme und eine Marke von HID, hat seinen Trends in Access Controllers Report 2026 veröffentlicht. Er zeigt, wie veränderte Anforderungen an die Cybersicherheit, Interoperabilität, Cloud-Nutzung und neue Technologien die Rolle der Controller in der langfristigen Strategie für die physische Zutrittskontrolle stärker in den Fokus rücken. Der Bericht basiert auf einer weltweiten Umfrage unter 561 Fachleuten aus den Bereichen physische Sicherheit und Cybersecurity. Dazu zählen Administratoren, die für das Management der Zutrittskontrolle zuständig sind, Systemintegratoren, Installateure und Endanwender. Dem Report nach halten 78 % der Befragten den Controller für wichtig oder gar entscheidend für ihre Strategie zum physischen Zutrittskontrollsystem (Physical Access Control System, kurz: PACS), 2025 waren es noch 72 %. Diese Entwicklung spiegelt die wachsende Rolle des Controllers im Sicherheitsumfeld wider, der immer mehr Geräte, Systeme und Anwendungen verbindet.
